transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ayesha (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Sunrise Head of ML), Rajiv (Infra), Tara (PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Discussed bursty traffic with long-tail token outputs for summarization and triage workflows.
- Agreed to provide replay traces and sample payloads; Redwood to share benchmark harness.
- Preliminary SLA targets: p50 <= 120ms for short hits, p95 <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms (subject to change after benchmark).

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ayesha: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to make sure we walk through the workload shape and get to an agreed set of success criteria for the POC. um quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: hi i'm maya, i lead the ml platform at sunrise, thanks for setting this up.
[00:16] Rajiv: rajiv infra, will be owning the cluster side and networking.
[00:20] Tara: tara product, i'll be tracking acceptance criteria and stakeholder comms.
[00:24] Diego: diego here, se on the redwood side, i'll dig into telemetry and benchmark details.
[00:29] Ayesha: cool, first question: high level what are the user journeys you want to exercise in the POC?
[00:35] Maya: two main ones. one is a short form triage API, think 8-40 token prompts for symptom classification, very low output token counts. second is a longer summarization flow, up to 800 tokens out on the response, so highly skewed token distribution.
[00:54] Tara: to add, the summarization is run on batches of docs from our ingestion pipeline, so there is some periodic bulk traffic during off-hours. also users occasionally trigger ad-hoc summarizations which create bursts.
[01:10] Ayesha: got it, so we need to plan for mixed QPS: steady small-query QPS and intermittent heavy-output bursts. could you give ballpark numbers?
[01:19] Maya: baseline QPS for the triage API is about 12 QPS, concurrency maybe 20 for short bursts, but we see spikes to ~200 qps during promotion events. for summaries, baseline is 0.5 qps but bursts up to 20 qps when bulk jobs start.
[01:36] Diego: that's helpful. do you have request size distributions? like input token histogram or output token CDF?
[01:42] Maya: we have logs but need to sanitize. typical input tokens: 6-50 tokens 88% of requests, remainder are long inputs up to 300 tokens. outputs: 70% under 40 tokens, 25% between 40 and 200, 5% long tails up to 800 tokens.
[02:01] Rajiv: important callout is that the long outputs are what drive VRAM/KV cache pressure, and they also increase per-token computation.
[02:08] Ayesha: yes exactly, that affects batching and kernel selection. for the POC we usually ask for a 7 day trace plus a small set of representative payloads so we can replay with weighted sampling.
[02:18] Tara: timeline wise we want a 3-week POC: week 1 replay + sizing, week 2 benchmarks, week 3 validation and reporting. is that reasonable from redwood side?
[02:29] Diego: that is doable, though if traces are messy it can push. we'll try to get a first-pass sizing within 2 business days after traces.
[02:36] Maya: what metrics should we expect in the benchmark deliverable?
[02:39] Diego: we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency for both short and long token classes, throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec), GPU utilization, token-level cost estimate, and KV cache hit/miss if applicable.
[02:50] Ayesha: also tail-latency heatmaps and concurrency quantiles so you can see where queueing happens.
[02:56] Rajiv: about network, we need to validate VPC connectivity and egress policies; if we run private deployment we'll need the security questionnaire answers up front.
[03:06] Ayesha: noted, we'll attach the security questionnaire and a summary of our compliance posture.
[03:10] Tara: any thoughts on SLA targets? our internal product wants p95 < 350ms for triage, but we guess that's ambitious.
[03:18] Diego: depends on model and batching. for short token hits with dedicated capacity and tuned batching something like p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300-400ms is in reach; p99 depends heavily on burst handling and autoscaling policy.
[03:30] Maya: can you explain how autoscaling and fallback policies work? we can't have long outages during bulk jobs.
[03:35] Ayesha: we have policies to spin up burst capacity and to fall back to a cheaper lower-capacity model variant if the primary can't keep up. fallback preserves availability but may change latency/quality. also we can route by region or capacity tier.
[03:50] Rajiv: fallback to lower-quality is a last resort; legal wants clear doc on what quality delta means.
[03:55] Ayesha: understood, we'll capture that in the runbook and include quality regression notes.
[04:00] Diego: on the technical side we should capture token mixes for replay: a 90/10 split short/long is what you're describing?
[04:06] Maya: roughly 88/12, but the long ones are the 5% tail of outputs and they dominate GPU time.
[04:12] Diego: right. so for the benchmark we'll generate a traffic replay with clusters of long-output requests interspersed with short queries to simulate realistic load. we'll also do a stress run where we amplify spikes 5x to see autoscaling response.
[04:26] Tara: what's the expected cost reporting? we need visibility into per-token and per-request cost for budgeting.
[04:31] Ayesha: we'll include token-level cost estimates and a breakdown by model, plus an ops run-rate estimate for dedicated capacity.
[04:37] Maya: about data residency and logs — we need audit logs stored for 1 year and access controls integrated with our SSO.
[04:44] Ayesha: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and audit logs; for private we can push logs to customer-owned S3 with KMS envelope keys. we'll attach the configuration doc.
[04:55] Rajiv: any limitations on replay fidelity? do you simulate KV cache warmup?
[04:59] Diego: we simulate prefix caching and allow a warmup phase; however, perfect fidelity is hard — sometimes transcribed prompts differ and the KV cache patterns vary. we'll document assumptions in the harness.
[05:10] Maya: ok. on success criteria — we want objective gates: 1) triage p95 <= 350ms under expected load, 2) summarize p95 <= 1.2s for heavy outputs, 3) no more than 1% error rate and successful run of 7 days of pipeline replay.
[05:27] Ayesha: sounds good. we might propose slightly different numbers after we run the baseline. recommend we make the success criteria conditional on model family and whether dedicated capacity is provisioned.
[05:38] Diego: one more thing — can you share sample payloads that include both short prompts and multi-document summarization so we can tune tokenization behavior?
[05:47] Maya: yes, we'll scrub PII and share sanitized examples.
[05:51] Tara: what's the format of the trace? we have json logs with timestamps and model id.
[05:55] Diego: json is ideal. include client id (hashed), prompt text, response length, timestamps; remove user identifiers.
[06:04] Rajiv: for network config we'll need a CIDR block and egress rules; can you provide a checklist?
[06:09] Ayesha: we'll send the VPC onboarding checklist and template for peering.
[06:13] Maya: any recommendations on model quantization for these mixes? we'd like to get small latency wins.
[06:18] Diego: quantization can help but long-output workloads may be limited by memory bandwidth; we'll include quantized and fp16 runs in benchmarks if you want.
[06:27] Ayesha: ok timeline recap: customer to send traces by 10/12, we run sizing and initial replay week of 10/13, bench week of 10/20, and deliver report by 11/01. is that acceptable?
[06:39] Maya: yes that timeline works.
[06:41] Tara: can you outline what will be in the final report?
[06:44] Diego: the report will have throughput/latency curves, token cost estimates, suggested cluster sizing for baseline and 2x burst, recommended batching and quantization settings, and a runbook for autoscaling/fallback.
[06:57] Rajiv: will you include GPU types in recommendations? we prefer to see NVLink vs PCIe tradeoffs.
[07:02] Diego: yes we will include recommended hardware profiles and expected utilization.
[07:06] Ayesha: ok let's capture action items.
[07:09] Tara: quick question — are there any rate limits we should expect from the hosted environment during the POC?
[07:15] Ayesha: for hosted tests we can increase quotas for the POC; for dedicated it's a non-issue. Diego will coordinate.
[07:22] {crosstalk}
[07:23] Diego: i'll add a note about quota increases.
[07:26] Maya: last item — security review, is SOC2 report available?
[07:30] Ayesha: yes we'll attach SOC2 Type II summary and a pointer to our compliance pack.
[07:33] Tara: great.
[07:35] Ayesha: thanks everyone. quick recap: Redwood to send benchmark template, VPC checklist, security docs; Customer to send traces and sample payloads; Redwood to return sizing and schedule workshop. next meeting tentatively 2027-10-14 to review sizing.
[07:51] Maya: thanks all.
[07:53] Rajiv: thanks.
[07:54] Diego: bye.

End of transcript.
